argument: Within Fréchet-distance-based distribution metrics used for per-condition evaluation of generative models, number of real samples available per evaluated condition is associated with stability of the estimated real-data mean and covariance used in the Fréchet distance under insufficient per-condition sample counts yield unstable estimates; hundreds to thousands of samples are typically required.
boundary: Evidence is limited to the reported PartNet part-tree setting and the Fréchet Point-cloud Distance evaluation procedure; transfer to other distributions or metrics is unestablished.
claim: Fréchet-distance-based distribution metrics require hundreds to thousands of real samples per evaluated condition to compute stable mean and covariance estimates; when per-condition real data are scarce, per-condition Fréchet distance estimates become unstable.
conditions: metric is computed per condition rather than over a pooled distribution
real-data mean and covariance are estimated from the available real samples
falsifier: Generate synthetic or resampled real feature distributions with varying per-condition sample sizes and measure the variance of the estimated Fréchet distance until stable estimates are obtained.
interpretation: The evidence supports a boundary or tradeoff concerning Fréchet-distance-based distribution metrics used for per-condition evaluation of generative models.
